## Definition

observable and probability postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4
and the identical-particle and spin postulate P6
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]), the radiation extension
postulate
[[post-nrqm-photons-radiation-extension-and-transverse-mode-assignment]] and
the static finite-level dipole postulate
[[post-nrqm-approximations-static-finite-level-dipole-coupling]], in the state
and outcome readings of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]] and
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], in the radiation
sector vocabulary of
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]] and
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]],
and in the units and dimensions of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the Axiom of Countable
Choice and the Axiom of Choice, the choice hypotheses of the cited Fock space
mathematics ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

**(b) Finite-level matter factor.** Take the declared charged pair, the
relative-coordinate factor $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$, the coordinate
multipliers $Q_{j}$ and the dipole operator components $D_{j}=-q\,Q_{j}$ of
[[post-nrqm-approximations-static-finite-level-dipole-coupling]] clauses
(i)-(ii), with the Coulomb energy operator $H_{\kappa}$ of clause (iv) of that
postulate. Fix, as model data, a declared finite-dimensional subspace
$$W\subseteq D(H_{\kappa})\cap D(Q_{1})\cap D(Q_{2})\cap D(Q_{3}),\qquad \dim W=d<\infty,$$
with a declared orthonormal basis $(w_{1},\dots,w_{d})$ of $W$
([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]),
and read $W$ as $\mathbb C^{d}$ in that basis. The model's **compressed matter
energy** is the Hermitian $d\times d$ matrix
$$H_{a}:=\Pi_{W}H_{\kappa}\big|_{W},$$
read in joules, where $\Pi_{W}$ is the orthogonal projection onto $W$
([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]); the model's **compressed dipole
matrices** are the Hermitian $d\times d$ matrices
$$D^{W}_{j}:=\Pi_{W}D_{j}\big|_{W}\qquad(j=1,2,3),$$
read in $\mathrm{C\,m}$; and the model's **levels** are the pairs $(E,v)$ with
$E\in\mathbb R$ (joules) an eigenvalue of $H_{a}$ and $v\in\mathbb C^{d}$ a
nonzero eigenvector for $E$. A **declared level pair** is an ordered pair
$(a,b)$ of orthonormal eigenvectors $v_{a},v_{b}$ of $H_{a}$; its **transition
energy** is $E_{a}-E_{b}$. The subspace, its basis and its dimension are model
data: they are not derived from the Coulomb model and they replace the
unbounded operators $H_{\kappa},D_{j}$ by their compressions throughout this
pair.

**(c) Radiation factor and cutoff dipole data.** Take the transverse
one-particle space $\mathfrak h$, the bosonic Fock space $F(\mathfrak h)$, the
vacuum $\Omega$, the sector projections $\Pi_{n}$ and the free-field energy
observable $H_{f}=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}T_{n}$ with $\varepsilon(k)=\hbar c|k|$ of
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]]
clauses (b),(d), with the domains and self-adjointness of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-transverse-continuum-free-fock-hamiltonian]]
and [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]], read in
joules. Fix, as further model data, a **cutoff** $\Lambda>0$ (joules), an
integer $J\ge1$ and vectors $g_{1},\dots,g_{J}\in\mathfrak h$ with
$$\operatorname{supp}g_{j}\subseteq\{k:\ 0<\varepsilon(k)\le\Lambda\},\qquad \frac{g_{j}}{\sqrt\varepsilon}\in\mathfrak h ,$$
and a real **coupling number** $\eta_{0}$ declared so that the interaction term
of clause (d) is read in joules. The cutoff and the mode vectors are model
data; no laboratory mode content, no Maxwell field, no mode density and no
value of $\eta_{0}$ is asserted.

**(d) The coupled model.** Write $\phi(g):=A_{-}(g)+A_{+}(g)$ for the maximal
creation-annihilation sum of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-closed-adjoint-sector-domains]] on
$F(\mathfrak h)$. The **declared finite-level cutoff dipole model** is the pair
of the Hilbert space $\mathbb C^{d}\otimes F(\mathfrak h)$
([[def-hilbert-space]]) and the operator
$$H_{\mathrm{LM}}:=H_{a}\otimes I+I\otimes H_{f}+\eta_{0}\sum_{j=1}^{J}D^{W}_{j}\otimes\phi(g_{j}), \qquad D(H_{\mathrm{LM}}):=\mathbb C^{d}\otimes D(H_{f}).$$

read with the Hermitian matrices $H_{a}$, $D^{W}_{1},\dots,D^{W}_{J}$ and the
coupling $\eta_{0}$ (its $d$ is the present $d$), the operator
$H_{\mathrm{LM}}$ is self-adjoint on the displayed domain and bounded below
([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]],
[[def-bounded-linear-operator]]). The model declares $H_{\mathrm{LM}}$ its
**energy observable**, in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], with energies,
mode energies and the coupling read in joules.

autonomous unitary family $U(t):=e^{-itH_{\mathrm{LM}}/\hbar}$, $t\in\mathbb R$,
in the reading of clause (iv) of P4 and of
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]; a preparation $\rho$ of
the model is a state of $\mathbb C^{d}\otimes F(\mathfrak h)$ in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], with
$\rho(t):=U(t)\rho U(t)^{*}$, and the outcome law of an assigned sharp
observable $(A,u_{A})$ is the reading of P2
([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). No
measurement, no detector, no environment, no external field, no rate and no
record is part of this definition.

**(f) Scope.** Clauses (b)-(e) are adopted model data and readings. They assert
nothing about a laboratory atom, sample, mode content, cutoff or coupling; no
Maxwell equation, source model, back-reaction or propagation is assumed; the
truncation, the cutoff and the mode vectors are not derived; and no
identification of $\eta_{0}$ or of the $g_{j}$ with laboratory quantities is
made. The identification of a physical preparation with a state of this model
is a tested identification with uncertainty under P7. The model contains no
photon detector, no sampling model, no environment beyond the declared
transverse modes, and no rate, decay or linewidth statement.

## Definition

**(a) Adopted readings.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the
observable and probability postulate P2, the ideal conditional-measurement
postulate P3 and the preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]), the finite-level cutoff
dipole model
[[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-finite-level-coupled-model]], the radiation
sector definition
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]] and
the declared ideal counting and energy-window detection models
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-ideal-counting-and-detection-model]], in the
readings of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]], with
the units of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the Axioms of
Countable Choice and of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

**(b) Declared level pair and transition energy.** A **declared level pair**
$(a,b)$ of the model is an ordered pair of orthonormal eigenvectors $v_{a},
v_{b}\in\mathbb C^{d}$ of the compressed matter energy $H_{a}$
([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]],
[[def-inner-product-space]]). Its **transition energy** is
$\Delta:=E_{a}-E_{b}$, read in joules; the pair is **upward** when
$\Delta>0$, meaning level $a$ lies above level $b$ in the model's energy
ordering.

**(c) Dipole coefficients and single-vertex photon density.** For an upward
declared level pair $(a,b)$ and the couplings $D^{W}_{j},g_{j},\eta_{0}$ of
[[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-finite-level-coupled-model]] clauses (c),(d),
the model's **dipole coefficients** are the complex numbers
$$c_{j}:=\bigl\langle D^{W}_{j}v_{a},\,v_{b}\bigr\rangle_{\mathbb C^{d}} \qquad(j=1,\dots,J),$$
the model's **single-vertex mode vector** is
$$M:=\sum_{j=1}^{J}c_{j}\,g_{j}\in\mathfrak h,$$
and the model's **single-vertex photon density** is the finite Borel measure on
$\mathbb R$
$$\nu_{b}(B):=\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}\mathbf 1_{B}\bigl(\varepsilon(k)\bigr)\, \|M(k)\|_{\mathbb C^{3}}^{2}\,d^{3}k,\qquad B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel},$$
read in the model's units and supported in $(0,\Lambda]$. The pairing is linear in its first argument and conjugate-linear in its
second. Thus $c_j$ is the actual coefficient of $v_b$ in $D_j^Wv_a$,
and Hermiticity gives $\langle D_j^Wv_b,v_a\rangle=\overline{c_j}$.
These are exactly the coefficients of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-golden-rule-coefficient-approximate-identity]]
clause (c), with no conjugation or change of the transverse mode vectors;
its mode vector and measure are the present $M$ and $\nu_b$.

**(d) Single-vertex emission vector and coefficient.** For $t\ge0$ the model's
**single-vertex emission vector** is the element of $\mathfrak h$
$$A_{b}(\cdot,t):\quad k\mapsto-\frac{i\eta_{0}}{\hbar}M(k) \int_{0}^{t}e^{i(\varepsilon(k)-\Delta)s/\hbar}\,ds ,$$
and the model's **single-vertex emission coefficient** is
$$\gamma_{b}(t):=\|A_{b}(\cdot,t)\|_{\mathfrak h}^{2}.$$
The vector and the coefficient are **defined model quantities**: the model
assigns them through this clause and through the cutoff dipole mathematics, and
they are not asserted to be the exact probability of any measurement of the
model. In particular $\gamma_{b}(t)$ is dimensionless and is not a rate; the
reading of a rate coefficient requires a separate limit statement, which is not
part of this definition.

**(e) Normalised single-vertex photon-energy law and ideal detection.** For
$t>0$ and $M\ne0$ the model's **normalised single-vertex photon-energy law** is
the Borel probability measure on $\mathbb R$
$$P_{b,t}(B):=\frac{\int_{B}K_{t}(E-\Delta)\,d\nu_{b}(E)} {\int_{\mathbb R}K_{t}(E-\Delta)\,d\nu_{b}(E)},\qquad K_{t}(x):=\frac{1}{\hbar^{2}t}\Bigl|\int_{0}^{t}e^{ixs/\hbar}\,ds\Bigr|^{2},$$
whose denominator is finite and strictly positive by
[[lem-nrqm-light-matter-first-order-photon-energy-law]] clause (b). This
probability law is defined independently of $\eta_0$, including $\eta_0=0$.
Its amplitude-based preparation reading additionally requires $A_b(\cdot,t)\ne0$.
For $t>0$ and $M\ne0$, this is equivalent to $\eta_0\ne0$, since
$\|A_b(\cdot,t)\|^2=\eta_0^2t\int K_t(E-\Delta)\,d\nu_b(E)$ and the integral
is positive. Under this condition the **declared single-vertex
one-photon preparation** is the unit vector $v_{b}\otimes(A_{b}(\cdot,t)/\|A_{b}(\cdot,t)\|_{\mathfrak h})$
of $\mathbb C^{d}\otimes\mathfrak h\subseteq\mathbb C^{d}\otimes
F(\mathfrak h)$, and for a Borel window $B\subseteq[0,\infty)$ the declared
ideal energy-window detector of window $B$ of
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-ideal-counting-and-detection-model]] clause (c)
has the Born probability $P_{b,t}(B)$ in that preparation, because the energy
law of a unit one-photon vector $f$ is the push-forward of
$\|f(k)\|_{\mathbb C^{3}}^{2}d^{3}k$ under $k\mapsto\varepsilon(k)$
([[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]] clause
(e)). When $\eta_0=0$, $A_b(\cdot,t)=0$ and no preparation obtained by
normalizing that emission amplitude is declared; the formal law $P_{b,t}$
remains the probability measure defined above. A **detected photon energy** is therefore a spectral reading of the
assigned free-field energy observable $(H_{f},\mathrm J)$, not a sharp energy
of a normalisable state and not a quantum number of the model's mode labels.

**(f) Scope.** Clauses (b)-(e) fix the model's spectral vocabulary. They assert
no sharp spectral line: the energy law of clause (e) is spread over the support
of $\nu_{b}$, and a point mass at $\Delta$ is only the idealisation proved as a
limit in [[lem-nrqm-light-matter-first-order-photon-energy-law]] clause (c).
They supply no spectrometer, no calibration, no detector response beyond the
declared ideal window, no efficiency, no background, no sampling model, no
count and no measurement record; the identification of a laboratory
spectrometer with a declared window is a tested identification with uncertainty
under P7. The single-vertex quantities of clauses (d)-(e) are conditional model
data; their relation to the model's exact outcome probabilities is a separate
proved statement.

## Facts & Assumptions

[F2] **Dyson expansion and tail.** With $V(t):=e^{itH_{0}/\hbar}Be^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}$ and the iterated integrals $\Psi_{n}(t)$ of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-vacuum-emission-dyson-convergence]] clause (b), the series $\sum_{n\ge0}\Psi_{n}(t)$ converges in the graph norm of $H_{f}$ uniformly for $t$ in compact sets, $e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}\sum_{n\ge0}\Psi_{n}(t)=e^{-itH_{\mathrm{LM}}/\hbar}\Psi_{0}$ for every $t\ge0$, and for $0\le t\le T$, $N\ge1$, $$\Bigl\|e^{-itH_{\mathrm{LM}}/\hbar}\Psi_{0}-e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}\Psi_{n}(t)\Bigr\|\le\sum_{n\ge N}\frac{(|\eta_{0}|Ct)^{n}}{\sqrt{n!}}$$ ([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-vacuum-emission-dyson-convergence]] clauses (b)-(d)); in particular, applying $e^{itH_{0}/\hbar}$ and taking $N=2$, $\|\Psi(t)-(\Psi_{0}+\Psi_{1}(t))\|\le\varepsilon_{2}(t)$ for $0\le t\le T$, where $\Psi(t):=e^{itH_{0}/\hbar}e^{-itH_{\mathrm{LM}}/\hbar}\Psi_{0}$.

[F3] **Spectral block of the free evolution.** $H_{0}(v_{a}\otimes\Omega)=E_{a}(v_{a}\otimes\Omega)$, and for $u\in\mathbb C^{d}$, $h\in\mathfrak h$, $j$ and real $s$, $e^{isH_{0}/\hbar}(D^{W}_{j}u\otimes g_{j})=e^{isH_{a}/\hbar}D^{W}_{j}u\otimes e^{is\varepsilon/\hbar}g_{j}$; moreover $\langle e^{isH_{a}/\hbar}D^{W}_{j}v_{a},v_{b}\rangle=e^{isE_{b}/\hbar}c_{j}$ and $\langle e^{isH_{a}/\hbar}D^{W}_{j}v_{b},v_{a}\rangle=e^{isE_{a}/\hbar}\overline{c_{j}}$, because $H_{a}v_{a}=E_{a}v_{a}$, $H_{a}v_{b}=E_{b}v_{b}$ and $D^{W}_{j}$ is Hermitian ([[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-finite-level-coupled-model]] clauses (b),(d), [[def-inner-product-space]], [[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]).

[F4] **One-photon sector and pairing.** $\Pi_{1}$ is the orthogonal projection of $F(\mathfrak h)$ onto the one-photon sector, the one-photon sector at level $d$ in $\mathbb C^{d}\otimes F(\mathfrak h)$ is $\mathbb C^{d}\otimes\operatorname{ran}\Pi_{1}$, whose level-$b$ part is $\mathbb C v_{b}\otimes\mathfrak h$; a vector $v_{b}\otimes f$ with $f\in\mathfrak h$ is paired by $\langle v_{b}\otimes f,v_{b}\otimes f'\rangle=\langle f,f'\rangle_{\mathfrak h}$ ([[lem-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fock-sector-projections]], [[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-inner-product-space]]).

[F6] **Projection probability comparison.** For arbitrary vectors $\psi,\varphi$ of a complex Hilbert space and an orthogonal projection $P$, $\bigl|\|P\psi\|^{2}-\|P\varphi\|^{2}\bigr|\le\|P(\psi-\varphi)\|\,(\|P\psi\|+\|P\varphi\|)\le\|\psi-\varphi\|(\|P\psi\|+\|P\varphi\|)$; and the model reads the probability of the spectral value $1$ of $(Q_{b},1)$ in a unit vector $\psi$ as $\|Q_{b}\psi\|^{2}$ ([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]], [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], [[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]], [[def-inner-product-space]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; evaluate the first interaction-picture Dyson term against the level-$b$ one-photon sector, compare the exact one-photon projection probability with the first-order coefficient through the Dyson tail, and compute the reverse-direction amplitude by the same expansion.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F7].

1.1 [The first Dyson term in the one-photon sector at level $b$] By [F1] and [F2], $\Psi_1(t)=-(i/\hbar)\int_0^tV(s)\Psi_0\,ds$ with $V(s)=e^{isH_0/\hbar}Be^{-isH_0/\hbar}$. The free initial phase is $e^{-isH_0/\hbar}\Psi_0=e^{-isE_a/\hbar}\Psi_0$, and $B\Psi_0=\eta_0\sum_jD_j^Wv_a\otimes g_j$. In the linear-first convention, the coefficient of $v_b$ in $e^{isH_a/\hbar}D_j^Wv_a$ is $\langle e^{isH_a/\hbar}D_j^Wv_a,v_b\rangle=e^{isE_b/\hbar}c_j$ by [F3]. Consequently $Q_bV(s)\Psi_0=v_b\otimes\eta_0 e^{-is\Delta/\hbar}e^{is\varepsilon/\hbar}M$. The bounded projection passes through the vector integral, giving $Q_b\Psi_1(t)=v_b\otimes[-(i\eta_0/\hbar)\int_0^te^{-is\Delta/\hbar}e^{is\varepsilon/\hbar}M\,ds]=v_b\otimes A_b(\cdot,t)$ by the definition of $A_b$. Equivalently, for every $f\in\mathfrak h$, $\langle\Psi_1(t),v_b\otimes f\rangle=\langle A_b(\cdot,t),f\rangle$, with all coefficients in the linear first slot. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F7, algebra]

2.1 [The coefficient] Clause (a) of [[lem-nrqm-light-matter-first-order-photon-energy-law]] with $t>0$ gives $\|A_{b}(\cdot,t)\|_{\mathfrak h}^{2}=\eta_{0}^{2}t\int K_{t}(E-\Delta)d\nu_{b}(E)$, which is $\gamma_{b}(t)$. This proves (a). [F5, step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 [Absorption mirror] For a unit $g\in\mathfrak h$, the first Dyson term with initial vector $\Phi_0=v_b\otimes g$ is well defined as a norm integral: the free evolution preserves the one-photon sector, and the creation/contraction bounds [F1] bound each vertex uniformly from that sector to the vacuum plus two-photon sectors. The sector maps are bounded and free evolution is strongly continuous, giving a norm-continuous integrand; these sector formulas supply the extension even when $g\notin D(\varepsilon)$. No full Dyson-series assertion for this initial vector is used. Set $h_s=e^{-is\varepsilon/\hbar}g$. The vacuum component of $\phi(g_j)h_s$ is $\langle h_s,g_j\rangle\Omega$ in the linear-first convention. The coefficient of $v_a$ in $e^{isH_a/\hbar}D_j^Wv_b$ is $e^{isE_a/\hbar}\overline{c_j}$ by [F3]; thus $\langle V(s)\Phi_0,v_a\otimes\Omega\rangle=\eta_0e^{is\Delta/\hbar}\sum_j\overline{c_j}\langle h_s,g_j\rangle=\eta_0e^{is\Delta/\hbar}\overline{\langle M,h_s\rangle}$. Integrating with $-i/\hbar$ in the first slot gives the displayed absorption amplitude. Step 1.1 and unitarity give $\alpha_{\mathrm{em}}=-(i\eta_0/\hbar)\int_0^te^{-is\Delta/\hbar}\langle e^{is\varepsilon/\hbar}M,g\rangle ds=-(i\eta_0/\hbar)\int_0^te^{-is\Delta/\hbar}\langle M,h_s\rangle ds$. Since $\eta_0$ is real, conjugating this scalar integral proves $\alpha_{\mathrm{abs}}=-\overline{\alpha_{\mathrm{em}}}$ and equal moduli, including $t=0$ or $\eta_0=0$. This proves (c) for the full complex couplings. [F1, F3, F4, F7, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 [Exact projection probability] Since $H_{0}$ commutes with $Q_{b}$ (both are diagonal in the level basis and $\Pi_1$ is the degree-one Fock-sector projection and the free field group preserves every particle-number sector, [F1], [F4]), [F2] gives $Q_{b}e^{-itH_{\mathrm{LM}}/\hbar}\Psi_{0}=Q_{b}e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}\Psi(t)=e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}Q_{b}\Psi(t)$, so $\|Q_{b}e^{-itH_{\mathrm{LM}}/\hbar}\Psi_{0}\|=\|Q_{b}\Psi(t)\|$ by unitarity. By [F2], $\|\Psi(t)-(\Psi_{0}+\Psi_{1}(t))\|\le\varepsilon_{2}(t)$, and $Q_{b}\Psi_{0}=0$ because $\Psi_{0}$ has no photons ([F4]), so $\|Q_{b}\Psi(t)-Q_{b}\Psi_{1}(t)\|\le\varepsilon_{2}(t)$. [F6] and step 1.1 then give $$\bigl|p_{b}(t)-\gamma_{b}(t)\bigr|\le\varepsilon_{2}(t)\bigl(2\|A_{b}(\cdot,t)\|_{\mathfrak h}+\varepsilon_{2}(t)\bigr),$$ since $\|Q_{b}\Psi_{1}(t)\|=\|A_{b}(\cdot,t)\|$ and $\|Q_{b}\Psi(t)\|\le\|A_{b}(\cdot,t)\|+\varepsilon_{2}(t)$. This proves (b). [F2, F4, F6, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 [Scope and assembly] Steps 1.1 and 2.1 prove (a), step 3.1 proves (b) and step 2.2 proves (c). Only the model's first-order Dyson terms, one projection probability and the finite interval $[0,T]$ entered; neither a rate, a decay, a linewidth, an environment nor a sampling model was formed, and no laboratory identification was made, which is (d). [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 3.1] ∎



## Remarks

- **Why the exact probability is not identified with the coefficient.** The projection $Q_{b}$ annihilates the vacuum and every sector of photon number different from one, but the Dyson terms of odd order $n\ge3$ can return to the one-photon sector; clause (b) therefore controls the exact probability by the tail rather than asserting equality. This is the explicit sense in which the single-vertex coefficient is a first-order model quantity.
- **The mirror is an algebraic identity, not a detailed-balance theorem.** Clause (c) relates the reverse first-order amplitudes of the same level pair and the same one-photon vector by $\alpha_{\mathrm{abs}}=-\overline{\alpha_{\mathrm{em}}}$. It assumes nothing about populations, temperatures or equilibrium; equality of moduli follows from the Hermitian coupling and the linear-first amplitude convention.

[F4] **One-photon sector and pairing.** $\Pi_{1}$ is the orthogonal projection of $F(\mathfrak h)$ onto the one-photon sector, the one-photon sector at level $d$ in $\mathbb C^{d}\otimes F(\mathfrak h)$ is $\mathbb C^{d}\otimes\operatorname{ran}\Pi_{1}$, whose level-$b$ part is $\mathbb C v_{b}\otimes\mathfrak h$; a vector $v_{b}\otimes f$ with $f\in\mathfrak h$ is paired by $\langle v_{b}\otimes f,v_{b}\otimes f'\rangle=\langle f,f'\rangle_{\mathfrak h}$ ([[lem-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fock-sector-projections]], [[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-inner-product-space]]).

[F5] **Kernel and coefficient.** $\gamma_{b}(t)=\|A_{b}(\cdot,t)\|_{\mathfrak h}^{2}=\eta_{0}^{2}t\int K_{t}(E-\Delta)d\nu_{b}(E)$ for $t>0$ and $A_{b}(\cdot,t)\in\mathfrak h$ ([[lem-nrqm-light-matter-first-order-photon-energy-law]] clause (a), [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-golden-rule-coefficient-approximate-identity]] clauses (ii),(iii)).

[F6] **Projection probability comparison.** For arbitrary vectors $\psi,\varphi$ of a complex Hilbert space and an orthogonal projection $P$, $\bigl|\|P\psi\|^{2}-\|P\varphi\|^{2}\bigr|\le\|P(\psi-\varphi)\|\,(\|P\psi\|+\|P\varphi\|)\le\|\psi-\varphi\|(\|P\psi\|+\|P\varphi\|)$; and the model reads the probability of the spectral value $1$ of $(Q_{b},1)$ in a unit vector $\psi$ as $\|Q_{b}\psi\|^{2}$ ([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]], [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], [[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]], [[def-inner-product-space]]).

[F7] **Framework readings.** Times and energies are read in seconds and joules as in [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]; $u\mapsto e^{is\varepsilon/\hbar}u$ is the unitary multiplication action of the one-particle energy on $\mathfrak h$ ([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-transverse-continuum-free-fock-hamiltonian]], [[def-bounded-linear-operator]], [[def-operator-norm]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; evaluate the first interaction-picture Dyson term against the level-$b$ one-photon sector, compare the exact one-photon projection probability with the first-order coefficient through the Dyson tail, and compute the reverse-direction amplitude by the same expansion.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F7].

1.1 [The first Dyson term in the one-photon sector at level $b$] By [F1] and [F2], $\Psi_1(t)=-(i/\hbar)\int_0^tV(s)\Psi_0\,ds$ with $V(s)=e^{isH_0/\hbar}Be^{-isH_0/\hbar}$. The free initial phase is $e^{-isH_0/\hbar}\Psi_0=e^{-isE_a/\hbar}\Psi_0$, and $B\Psi_0=\eta_0\sum_jD_j^{\mathrm{ch}}v_a\otimes g_j$. In the linear-first convention, the coefficient of $v_b$ in $e^{isH_a/\hbar}D_j^{\mathrm{ch}}v_a$ is $\langle e^{isH_a/\hbar}D_j^{\mathrm{ch}}v_a,v_b\rangle=e^{isE_b/\hbar}c_j$ by [F3]. Consequently $Q_bV(s)\Psi_0=v_b\otimes\eta_0 e^{-is\Delta/\hbar}e^{is\varepsilon/\hbar}M$. The bounded projection passes through the vector integral, giving $Q_b\Psi_1(t)=v_b\otimes[-(i\eta_0/\hbar)\int_0^te^{-is\Delta/\hbar}e^{is\varepsilon/\hbar}M\,ds]=v_b\otimes A_b(\cdot,t)$ by the definition of $A_b$. Equivalently, for every $f\in\mathfrak h$, $\langle\Psi_1(t),v_b\otimes f\rangle=\langle A_b(\cdot,t),f\rangle$, with all coefficients in the linear first slot. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F7, algebra]

The sector maps are bounded and free evolution is strongly continuous, giving a norm-continuous integrand; these sector formulas supply the extension even when $g\notin D(\varepsilon)$. No full Dyson-series assertion for this initial vector is used. Set $h_s=e^{-is\varepsilon/\hbar}g$. The vacuum component of $\phi(g_j)h_s$ is $\langle h_s,g_j\rangle\Omega$ in the linear-first convention. The coefficient of $v_a$ in $e^{isH_a/\hbar}D_j^{\mathrm{ch}}v_b$ is $e^{isE_a/\hbar}\overline{c_j}$ by [F3]; thus $\langle V(s)\Phi_0,v_a\otimes\Omega\rangle=\eta_0e^{is\Delta/\hbar}\sum_j\overline{c_j}\langle h_s,g_j\rangle=\eta_0e^{is\Delta/\hbar}\overline{\langle M,h_s\rangle}$. Integrating with $-i/\hbar$ in the first slot gives the displayed absorption amplitude. Step 1.1 and unitarity give $\alpha_{\mathrm{em}}=-(i\eta_0/\hbar)\int_0^te^{-is\Delta/\hbar}\langle e^{is\varepsilon/\hbar}M,g\rangle ds=-(i\eta_0/\hbar)\int_0^te^{-is\Delta/\hbar}\langle M,h_s\rangle ds$. Since $\eta_0$ is real, conjugating this scalar integral proves $\alpha_{\mathrm{abs}}=-\overline{\alpha_{\mathrm{em}}}$ and equal moduli, including $t=0$ or $\eta_0=0$. This proves (c) for the full complex couplings. [F1, F3, F4, F7, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 [Exact projection probability] Since $H_{0}$ commutes with $Q_{b}$ (both are diagonal in the level basis and $\Pi_1$ is the degree-one Fock-sector projection and the free field group preserves every particle-number sector, [F1], [F4]), [F2] gives $Q_{b}e^{-itH_{\mathrm{LM}}/\hbar}\Psi_{0}=Q_{b}e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}\Psi(t)=e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}Q_{b}\Psi(t)$, so $\|Q_{b}e^{-itH_{\mathrm{LM}}/\hbar}\Psi_{0}\|=\|Q_{b}\Psi(t)\|$ by unitarity. By [F2], $\|\Psi(t)-(\Psi_{0}+\Psi_{1}(t))\|\le\varepsilon_{2}(t)$, and $Q_{b}\Psi_{0}=0$ because $\Psi_{0}$ has no photons ([F4]), so $\|Q_{b}\Psi(t)-Q_{b}\Psi_{1}(t)\|\le\varepsilon_{2}(t)$. [F6] and step 1.1 then give $$\bigl|p_{b}(t)-\gamma_{b}(t)\bigr|\le\varepsilon_{2}(t)\bigl(2\|A_{b}(\cdot,t)\|_{\mathfrak h}+\varepsilon_{2}(t)\bigr),$$ since $\|Q_{b}\Psi_{1}(t)\|=\|A_{b}(\cdot,t)\|$ and $\|Q_{b}\Psi(t)\|\le\|A_{b}(\cdot,t)\|+\varepsilon_{2}(t)$. This proves (b). [F2, F4, F6, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 [Scope and assembly] Steps 1.1 and 2.1 prove (a), step 3.1 proves (b) and step 2.2 proves (c). Only the model's first-order Dyson terms, one projection probability and the finite interval $[0,T]$ entered; neither a rate, a decay, a linewidth, an environment nor a sampling model was formed, and no laboratory identification was made, which is (d). [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 3.1] ∎



## Remarks

- **Why the exact probability is not identified with the coefficient.** The projection $Q_{b}$ annihilates the vacuum and every sector of photon number different from one, but the Dyson terms of odd order $n\ge3$ can return to the one-photon sector; clause (b) therefore controls the exact probability by the tail rather than asserting equality. This is the explicit sense in which the single-vertex coefficient is a first-order model quantity.
- **The mirror is an algebraic identity, not a detailed-balance theorem.** Clause (c) relates the reverse first-order amplitudes of the same level pair and the same one-photon vector by $\alpha_{\mathrm{abs}}=-\overline{\alpha_{\mathrm{em}}}$. It assumes nothing about populations, temperatures or equilibrium; equality of moduli follows from the Hermitian coupling and the linear-first amplitude convention.

## Statement

Adopt the declared finite-level cutoff dipole model
[[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-finite-level-coupled-model]] and its
spectral-transition reading
[[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-spectral-transition-and-detection]], the
declared ideal energy-window detection model
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-ideal-counting-and-detection-model]] clause (c)
and the preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]). Assume the Axioms of
Countable Choice and of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Declare **three models**, all with the same matter
data $H_{a}$, $D^{W}_{j}$ and the same cutoff $\Lambda$ and coupling
$\eta_{0}$, and with a declared upward level pair $(a,b)$, $\Delta\in(0,\Lambda)$:

1. model $M_{1}$: cutoff mode data whose single-vertex photon density is
   $\nu^{(1)}_{b}=J_{1}\lambda$ with $J_{1}\in L^{1}(\lambda)$, $J_{1}=0$
   $\lambda$-almost everywhere off $(0,\Lambda]$ and $J_{1}$ continuous at
   $\Delta$ with $J_{1}(\Delta)>0$;
2. model $M_{2}$: same matter and cutoff data, single-vertex photon density
   $\nu^{(2)}_{b}=J_{2}\lambda$, $J_{2}$ with the same properties and
   $J_{2}(\Delta)=J_{1}(\Delta)$;
3. model $L$ (the **declared ideal sharp-line model**): a declared spectral
   model in which the energy of an emitted and detected quantum is the value
   $\Delta$ with probability one, so that every energy window
   $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ has probability $\mathbf 1_{B}(\Delta)$.

Assume in addition that $J_{1}$ and $J_{2}$ are **not proportional**: there is
no $\gamma\ge0$ with $J_{1}=\gamma J_{2}$ $\lambda$-almost everywhere. Then:

(a) (equal rate coefficients) the model rate coefficients of clause (c) of
[[pthm-nrqm-light-matter-golden-rule-limit-and-rate-reading]] coincide,
$$\Gamma_{1}=\frac{2\pi\eta_{0}^{2}}{\hbar}J_{1}(\Delta) =\frac{2\pi\eta_{0}^{2}}{\hbar}J_{2}(\Delta)=\Gamma_{2};$$
in particular a comparison of the leading rate coefficients alone does not
discriminate $M_{1}$ from $M_{2}$;

(b) (different detected-energy laws) for every $t>0$ the normalised
single-vertex photon-energy laws $P^{(1)}_{t}$ and $P^{(2)}_{t}$ of clause (e)
of [[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-spectral-transition-and-detection]]
differ: there is a Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ with
$P^{(1)}_{t}(B)\ne P^{(2)}_{t}(B)$; consequently an energy-resolved comparison
that resolves the difference between $J_{1}$ and $J_{2}$ discriminates $M_{1}$
from $M_{2}$, while the rate comparison of (a) does not;

(c) (the sharp line is a limit, not a finite-time property) if $J_{1}>0$
$\lambda$-almost everywhere on a Borel set $B$ of positive Lebesgue measure
with $\Delta\notin B$, then $P^{(1)}_{t}(B)>0$ for every $t>0$ whereas
$L$ assigns probability $0$ to $B$; on the other hand
$P^{(1)}_{t}(B)\to0$ as $t\to\infty$ for every Borel $B$ bounded away from
$\Delta$. Thus the declared sharp-line model is the idealisation that the
single-vertex law approaches in the limit, not a property of the
finite-time law;

(d) (what the comparison is) clauses (a)-(c) are statements about the three
declared models. They construct no laboratory comparison and report no data:
no apparatus, preparation, calibration, detector response, efficiency,
background, trial count, frequency or uncertainty budget is supplied, and
none is invented. Comparing any of these predictions with reported data would
test the combined model and apparatus assumptions under P7, would require a
declared sampling and measurement model, and would carry finite-sample
fluctuations and systematic uncertainties; it would not prove a model.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the three declared models $M_{1},M_{2},L$ with their data and densities $J_{1},J_{2}$, the level pair $(a,b)$ and $\Delta\in(0,\Lambda)$, the rate coefficients $\Gamma_{1},\Gamma_{2}$, the laws $P^{(1)}_{t},P^{(2)}_{t}$ and a Borel window $B$; the cited suppliers.

[F1] **Rate coefficients.** Under the stated density hypotheses on $J_{i}$ the rate coefficients exist and equal $\frac{2\pi\eta_{0}^{2}}{\hbar}J_{i}(\Delta)$ ([[pthm-nrqm-light-matter-golden-rule-limit-and-rate-reading]] clauses (a),(c); [[lem-nrqm-light-matter-first-order-photon-energy-law]]).

[F2] **Energy laws and kernel.** For model $i$ and $t>0$, $P^{(i)}_{t}(B)=\int_{B}K_{t}(E-\Delta)J_{i}(E)\,d\lambda(E)\big/\int_{\mathbb R}K_{t}(E-\Delta)J_{i}(E)\,d\lambda(E)$, the denominator is finite and positive, $K_{t}>0$ $\lambda$-almost everywhere, and $P^{(i)}_{t}(B)>0$ for every Borel $B$ of positive measure on which $J_{i}>0$ almost everywhere ([[lem-nrqm-light-matter-first-order-photon-energy-law]] clauses (b),(d); [[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-spectral-transition-and-detection]] clause (e); [[def-measure-with-density]]).

[F3] **Tail concentration and density identity.** Under the density hypotheses of [F1], for every $\delta>0$, $P^{(i)}_{t}(\{|E-\Delta|\ge\delta\})\to0$ as $t\to\infty$; and the identity $P^{(1)}_{t}=P^{(2)}_{t}$ for a fixed $t$ is equivalent to $K_{t}(E-\Delta)J_{1}(E)=c\,K_{t}(E-\Delta)J_{2}(E)$ $\lambda$-almost everywhere for $c:=\int K_{t}(\cdot-\Delta)J_{1}d\lambda/\int K_{t}(\cdot-\Delta)J_{2}d\lambda$ ([[lem-nrqm-light-matter-first-order-photon-energy-law]] clauses (c),(e); [[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]], [[def-measure-with-density]]).

[F4] **Detection reading.** For a unit one-photon vector the energy law and the ideal energy-window probability are the readings of [[def-nrqm-photons-framework-ideal-counting-and-detection-model]] clause (c) and [[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-spectral-transition-and-detection]] clause (e); the sharp-line model $L$ is a declared model whose law assigns $\mathbf 1_{B}(\Delta)$ to a window $B$, and it is not asserted to arise from any density $J\in L^{1}(\lambda)$.

[F5] **Prediction versus comparison.** The outcome law of a declared measurement is a single-trial model prediction; a comparison with data requires a declared sampling and measurement model, and agreement is evidence for the combined assumptions, not a proof ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]], [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]], [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; compare the two rate coefficients, show that the two energy laws differ by the positivity of the kernel, and locate the sharp-line model in the limit using tail concentration.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F5].

1.2 [The laws differ] Fix $t>0$ and let $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ be Borel. By [F2], the equality $P^{(1)}_{t}(B)=P^{(2)}_{t}(B)$ for all Borel $B$ would give $K_{t}(E-\Delta)J_{1}(E)=cK_{t}(E-\Delta)J_{2}(E)$ $\lambda$-almost everywhere with $c>0$ as in [F3], and since $K_{t}>0$ $\lambda$-almost everywhere by [F2], division yields $J_{1}=cJ_{2}$ $\lambda$-almost everywhere, contradicting the hypothesis that the densities are not proportional; hence some Borel $B$ separates the two laws. $\lambda$-almost everywhere on a Borel set $B$ of positive Lebesgue measure

after.claim: [The first Dyson term in the one-photon sector at level $b$] By [F1] and [F2], $\Psi_1(t)=-(i/\hbar)\int_0^tV(s)\Psi_0\,ds$ with $V(s)=e^{isH_0/\hbar}Be^{-isH_0/\hbar}$. The free initial phase is $e^{-isH_0/\hbar}\Psi_0=e^{-isE_a/\hbar}\Psi_0$, and $B\Psi_0=\eta_0\sum_jD_j^{\mathrm{ch}}v_a\otimes g_j$. In the linear-first convention, the coefficient of $v_b$ in $e^{isH_a/\hbar}D_j^{\mathrm{ch}}v_a$ is $\langle e^{isH_a/\hbar}D_j^{\mathrm{ch}}v_a,v_b\rangle=e^{isE_b/\hbar}c_j$ by [F3]. Consequently $Q_bV(s)\Psi_0=v_b\otimes\eta_0 e^{-is\Delta/\hbar}e^{is\varepsilon/\hbar}M$. The bounded projection passes through the vector integral, giving $Q_b\Psi_1(t)=v_b\otimes[-(i\eta_0/\hbar)\int_0^te^{-is\Delta/\hbar}e^{is\varepsilon/\hbar}M\,ds]=v_b\otimes A_b(\cdot,t)$ by the definition of $A_b$. Equivalently, for every $f\in\mathfrak h$, $\langle\Psi_1(t),v_b\otimes f\rangle=\langle A_b(\cdot,t),f\rangle$, with all coefficients in the linear first slot.

[The coefficient] Clause (a) of [[lem-nrqm-light-matter-first-order-photon-energy-law]] with $t>0$ gives $\|A_{b}(\cdot,t)\|_{\mathfrak h}^{2}=\eta_{0}^{2}t\int K_{t}(E-\Delta)d\nu_{b}(E)$, which is $\gamma_{b}(t)$. This proves (a).

[Absorption mirror] For a unit $g\in\mathfrak h$, the first Dyson term with initial vector $\Phi_0=v_b\otimes g$ is well defined as a norm integral: the free evolution preserves the one-photon sector, and the creation/contraction bounds [F1] bound each vertex uniformly from that sector to the vacuum plus two-photon sectors. The sector maps are bounded and free evolution is strongly continuous, giving a norm-continuous integrand; these sector formulas supply the extension even when $g\notin D(\varepsilon)$. No full Dyson-series assertion for this initial vector is used. Set $h_s=e^{-is\varepsilon/\hbar}g$. The vacuum component of $\phi(g_j)h_s$ is $\langle h_s,g_j\rangle\Omega$ in the linear-first convention. The coefficient of $v_a$ in $e^{isH_a/\hbar}D_j^{\mathrm{ch}}v_b$ is $e^{isE_a/\hbar}\overline{c_j}$ by [F3]; thus $\langle V(s)\Phi_0,v_a\otimes\Omega\rangle=\eta_0e^{is\Delta/\hbar}\sum_j\overline{c_j}\langle h_s,g_j\rangle=\eta_0e^{is\Delta/\hbar}\overline{\langle M,h_s\rangle}$. Integrating with $-i/\hbar$ in the first slot gives the displayed absorption amplitude. Step 1.1 and unitarity give $\alpha_{\mathrm{em}}=-(i\eta_0/\hbar)\int_0^te^{-is\Delta/\hbar}\langle e^{is\varepsilon/\hbar}M,g\rangle ds=-(i\eta_0/\hbar)\int_0^te^{-is\Delta/\hbar}\langle M,h_s\rangle ds$. Since $\eta_0$ is real, conjugating this scalar integral proves $\alpha_{\mathrm{abs}}=-\overline{\alpha_{\mathrm{em}}}$ and equal moduli, including $t=0$ or $\eta_0=0$. This proves (c) for the full complex couplings.

[Exact projection probability] Since $H_{0}$ commutes with $Q_{b}$ (both are diagonal in the level basis and $\Pi_1$ is the degree-one Fock-sector projection and the free field group preserves every particle-number sector, [F1], [F4]), [F2] gives $Q_{b}e^{-itH_{\mathrm{LM}}/\hbar}\Psi_{0}=Q_{b}e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}\Psi(t)=e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}Q_{b}\Psi(t)$, so $\|Q_{b}e^{-itH_{\mathrm{LM}}/\hbar}\Psi_{0}\|=\|Q_{b}\Psi(t)\|$ by unitarity. By [F2], $\|\Psi(t)-(\Psi_{0}+\Psi_{1}(t))\|\le\varepsilon_{2}(t)$, and $Q_{b}\Psi_{0}=0$ because $\Psi_{0}$ has no photons ([F4]), so $\|Q_{b}\Psi(t)-Q_{b}\Psi_{1}(t)\|\le\varepsilon_{2}(t)$. [F6] and step 1.1 then give $$\bigl|p_{b}(t)-\gamma_{b}(t)\bigr|\le\varepsilon_{2}(t)\bigl(2\|A_{b}(\cdot,t)\|_{\mathfrak h}+\varepsilon_{2}(t)\bigr),$$ since $\|Q_{b}\Psi_{1}(t)\|=\|A_{b}(\cdot,t)\|$ and $\|Q_{b}\Psi(t)\|\le\|A_{b}(\cdot,t)\|+\varepsilon_{2}(t)$. This proves (b).

[Scope and assembly] Steps 1.1 and 2.1 prove (a), step 3.1 proves (b) and step 2.2 proves (c). Only the model's first-order Dyson terms, one projection probability and the finite interval $[0,T]$ entered; neither a rate, a decay, a linewidth, an environment nor a sampling model was formed, and no laboratory identification was made, which is (d).

coefficients $c_{j}=\langle D^{W}_{j}v_{a},v_{b}\rangle$, mode vector $M$ and
photon density $\nu_{b}$ of
[[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-spectral-transition-and-detection]] clauses
(b),(c). Write $H_{0}:=H_{a}\otimes I+I\otimes H_{f}$ and
$B:=\eta_{0}\sum_{j}D^{W}_{j}\otimes\phi(g_{j})$, so that $H_{\mathrm{LM}}=H_{0}+B$
on $\mathbb C^{d}\otimes D(H_{f})$. Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and
of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix $T>0$,
put
$$C:=\frac{2}{\hbar}\sum_{j=1}^{J}\|D^{W}_{j}\|\,\|g_{j}\|_{\mathfrak h}, \qquad \varepsilon_{2}(t):=\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{(|\eta_{0}|Ct)^{n}}{\sqrt{n!}}\qquad(0\le t\le T),$$
and let $\Psi_{0}:=v_{a}\otimes\Omega$. For $t\ge0$ let $\Psi_{1}(t)$ denote the
first interaction-picture Dyson term of the model with initial vector
$\Psi_{0}$, as in
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-vacuum-emission-dyson-convergence]] clause (b).

(a) (single-vertex emission vector) the component of $\Psi_{1}(t)$ in the
one-photon sector at level $b$ is
$$v_{b}\otimes A_{b}(\cdot,t),$$
with $A_{b}(\cdot,t)$ the single-vertex emission vector of
[[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-spectral-transition-and-detection]] clause
(d) and
[[lem-nrqm-light-matter-first-order-photon-energy-law]]; consequently the
single-vertex emission coefficient of the model is
$$\gamma_{b}(t)=\eta_{0}^{2}\,t\int_{\mathbb R}K_{t}(E-\Delta)\,d\nu_{b}(E) \qquad(t>0);$$

(b) (exact model probability up to the Dyson tail) let
$Q_{b}:=|v_{b}\rangle\langle v_{b}|\otimes\Pi_{1}$ and let
$$p_{b}(t):=\|Q_{b}\,e^{-itH_{\mathrm{LM}}/\hbar}\Psi_{0}\|^{2}$$
be the model's probability of the spectral value $1$ of the assigned sharp
observable $(Q_{b},1)$ in the evolved preparation of $\Psi_{0}$ at time $t$
(the reading of P2, [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). Then for
$0\le t\le T$,
$$\bigl|p_{b}(t)-\gamma_{b}(t)\bigr|\le \varepsilon_{2}(t)\bigl(2\|A_{b}(\cdot,t)\|_{\mathfrak h}+\varepsilon_{2}(t)\bigr);$$
in particular the exact probability equals the single-vertex coefficient up to
the explicit Dyson tail, which is not asserted to be small;

(c) (absorption mirror) let $g\in\mathfrak h$ be a unit vector, let
$\Psi_1^g(t)$ be the first interaction-picture Dyson term with initial
vector $\Phi_0=v_b\otimes g$, defined as a norm integral using the
finite-photon-sector creation/contraction action, and define the physical
transition amplitudes with the output vector in the first slot,
$$\alpha_{\mathrm{em}}(t):=\langle\Psi_1(t),v_b\otimes g\rangle,\qquad \alpha_{\mathrm{abs}}(t):=\langle\Psi_1^g(t),v_a\otimes\Omega\rangle.$$
Then for every $t\ge0$,
$$\alpha_{\mathrm{em}}(t)=-\frac{i\eta_0}{\hbar}\int_0^te^{-i\Delta s/\hbar}\langle M,e^{-is\varepsilon/\hbar}g\rangle_{\mathfrak h}\,ds,\qquad \alpha_{\mathrm{abs}}(t)=-\frac{i\eta_0}{\hbar}\int_0^te^{+i\Delta s/\hbar}\overline{\langle M,e^{-is\varepsilon/\hbar}g\rangle_{\mathfrak h}}\,ds,$$
and hence
$$\alpha_{\mathrm{abs}}(t)=-\overline{\alpha_{\mathrm{em}}(t)},\qquad |\alpha_{\mathrm{abs}}(t)|=|\alpha_{\mathrm{em}}(t)|.$$
This compares the reverse transitions for the same level pair, the same
unit one-photon vector $g$ and the same real coupling $\eta_0$, retaining
arbitrary complex Hermitian dipole matrices and transverse mode vectors;

(d) (scope) clauses (a)-(c) are statements about the model's first-order Dyson
terms and about one projection probability of the exact model evolution. No
rate, exponential decay, linewidth, environment, sampling model or measurement
record is asserted; the identification of a laboratory preparation with
$\Psi_{0}$ and of a laboratory detector with the observable $Q_{b}$ is a tested
identification with uncertainty under P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]); and no value of
$\eta_{0}$, $D^{W}_{j}$, $g_{j}$ or $\Lambda$ is asserted.

proved statement.

claim.text:
Adopt the model of
[[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-finite-level-coupled-model]] with its data
$d$, $H_{a}$, $D_j^{\mathrm{ch}}$, $\Lambda$, $g_{j}$, $\eta_{0}$, and a declared upward
level pair $(a,b)$ with transition energy $\Delta=E_{a}-E_{b}>0$ and page
coefficients $c_{j}=\langle D_j^{\mathrm{ch}}v_{a},v_{b}\rangle$, mode vector $M$ and
photon density $\nu_{b}$ of
[[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-spectral-transition-and-detection]] clauses
(b),(c). Write $H_{0}:=H_{a}\otimes I+I\otimes H_{f}$ and
$B:=\eta_{0}\sum_{j}D_j^{\mathrm{ch}}\otimes\phi(g_{j})$, so that $H_{\mathrm{LM}}=H_{0}+B$
on $\mathbb C^{d}\otimes D(H_{f})$. Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and
of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix $T>0$,
put
$$C:=\frac{2}{\hbar}\sum_{j=1}^{J}\|D_j^{\mathrm{ch}}\|\,\|g_{j}\|_{\mathfrak h}, \qquad \varepsilon_{2}(t):=\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{(|\eta_{0}|Ct)^{n}}{\sqrt{n!}}\qquad(0\le t\le T),$$
and let $\Psi_{0}:=v_{a}\otimes\Omega$. For $t\ge0$ let $\Psi_{1}(t)$ denote the
first interaction-picture Dyson term of the model with initial vector
$\Psi_{0}$, as in
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-vacuum-emission-dyson-convergence]] clause (b).
Then:

(a) (single-vertex emission vector) the component of $\Psi_{1}(t)$ in the
one-photon sector at level $b$ is
$$v_{b}\otimes A_{b}(\cdot,t),$$
with $A_{b}(\cdot,t)$ the single-vertex emission vector of
[[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-spectral-transition-and-detection]] clause
(d) and
[[lem-nrqm-light-matter-first-order-photon-energy-law]]; consequently the
single-vertex emission coefficient of the model is
$$\gamma_{b}(t)=\eta_{0}^{2}\,t\int_{\mathbb R}K_{t}(E-\Delta)\,d\nu_{b}(E) \qquad(t>0);$$

(b) (exact model probability up to the Dyson tail) let
$Q_{b}:=|v_{b}\rangle\langle v_{b}|\otimes\Pi_{1}$ and let
$$p_{b}(t):=\|Q_{b}\,e^{-itH_{\mathrm{LM}}/\hbar}\Psi_{0}\|^{2}$$
be the model's probability of the spectral value $1$ of the assigned sharp
observable $(Q_{b},1)$ in the evolved preparation of $\Psi_{0}$ at time $t$
(the reading of P2, [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). Then for
$0\le t\le T$,
$$\bigl|p_{b}(t)-\gamma_{b}(t)\bigr|\le \varepsilon_{2}(t)\bigl(2\|A_{b}(\cdot,t)\|_{\mathfrak h}+\varepsilon_{2}(t)\bigr);$$
in particular the exact probability equals the single-vertex coefficient up to
the explicit Dyson tail, which is not asserted to be small;

(c) (absorption mirror) let $g\in\mathfrak h$ be a unit vector, let
$\Psi_1^g(t)$ be the first interaction-picture Dyson term with initial
vector $\Phi_0=v_b\otimes g$, defined as a norm integral using the
finite-photon-sector creation/contraction action, and define the physical
transition amplitudes with the output vector in the first slot,
$$\alpha_{\mathrm{em}}(t):=\langle\Psi_1(t),v_b\otimes g\rangle,\qquad \alpha_{\mathrm{abs}}(t):=\langle\Psi_1^g(t),v_a\otimes\Omega\rangle.$$
Then for every $t\ge0$,
$$\alpha_{\mathrm{em}}(t)=-\frac{i\eta_0}{\hbar}\int_0^te^{-i\Delta s/\hbar}\langle M,e^{-is\varepsilon/\hbar}g\rangle_{\mathfrak h}\,ds,\qquad \alpha_{\mathrm{abs}}(t)=-\frac{i\eta_0}{\hbar}\int_0^te^{+i\Delta s/\hbar}\overline{\langle M,e^{-is\varepsilon/\hbar}g\rangle_{\mathfrak h}}\,ds,$$
and hence
$$\alpha_{\mathrm{abs}}(t)=-\overline{\alpha_{\mathrm{em}}(t)},\qquad |\alpha_{\mathrm{abs}}(t)|=|\alpha_{\mathrm{em}}(t)|.$$
This compares the reverse transitions for the same level pair, the same
unit one-photon vector $g$ and the same real coupling $\eta_0$, retaining
arbitrary complex Hermitian dipole matrices and transverse mode vectors;

(d) (scope) clauses (a)-(c) are statements about the model's first-order Dyson
terms and about one projection probability of the exact model evolution. No
rate, exponential decay, linewidth, environment, sampling model or measurement
record is asserted; the identification of a laboratory preparation with
$\Psi_{0}$ and of a laboratory detector with the observable $Q_{b}$ is a tested
identification with uncertainty under P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]); and no value of
$\eta_{0}$, $D_j^{\mathrm{ch}}$, $g_{j}$ or $\Lambda$ is asserted.

current_steps.quote: [The first Dyson term in the one-photon sector at level $b$] By [F1] and [F2], $\Psi_1(t)=-(i/\hbar)\int_0^tV(s)\Psi_0\,ds$ with $V(s)=e^{isH_0/\hbar}Be^{-isH_0/\hbar}$. The free initial phase is $e^{-isH_0/\hbar}\Psi_0=e^{-isE_a/\hbar}\Psi_0$, and $B\Psi_0=\eta_0\sum_jD_j^{\mathrm{ch}}v_a\otimes g_j$. In the linear-first convention, the coefficient of $v_b$ in $e^{isH_a/\hbar}D_j^{\mathrm{ch}}v_a$ is $\langle e^{isH_a/\hbar}D_j^{\mathrm{ch}}v_a,v_b\rangle=e^{isE_b/\hbar}c_j$ by [F3]. Consequently $Q_bV(s)\Psi_0=v_b\otimes\eta_0 e^{-is\Delta/\hbar}e^{is\varepsilon/\hbar}M$. The bounded projection passes through the vector integral, giving $Q_b\Psi_1(t)=v_b\otimes[-(i\eta_0/\hbar)\int_0^te^{-is\Delta/\hbar}e^{is\varepsilon/\hbar}M\,ds]=v_b\otimes A_b(\cdot,t)$ by the definition of $A_b$. Equivalently, for every $f\in\mathfrak h$, $\langle\Psi_1(t),v_b\otimes f\rangle=\langle A_b(\cdot,t),f\rangle$, with all coefficients in the linear first slot. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F7, algebra]

[The coefficient] Clause (a) of [[lem-nrqm-light-matter-first-order-photon-energy-law]] with $t>0$ gives $\|A_{b}(\cdot,t)\|_{\mathfrak h}^{2}=\eta_{0}^{2}t\int K_{t}(E-\Delta)d\nu_{b}(E)$, which is $\gamma_{b}(t)$. This proves (a). [F5, step 1.1, algebra]

[Absorption mirror] For a unit $g\in\mathfrak h$, the first Dyson term with initial vector $\Phi_0=v_b\otimes g$ is well defined as a norm integral: the free evolution preserves the one-photon sector, and the creation/contraction bounds [F1] bound each vertex uniformly from that sector to the vacuum plus two-photon sectors. The sector maps are bounded and free evolution is strongly continuous, giving a norm-continuous integrand; these sector formulas supply the extension even when $g\notin D(\varepsilon)$. No full Dyson-series assertion for this initial vector is used. Set $h_s=e^{-is\varepsilon/\hbar}g$. The vacuum component of $\phi(g_j)h_s$ is $\langle h_s,g_j\rangle\Omega$ in the linear-first convention. The coefficient of $v_a$ in $e^{isH_a/\hbar}D_j^{\mathrm{ch}}v_b$ is $e^{isE_a/\hbar}\overline{c_j}$ by [F3]; thus $\langle V(s)\Phi_0,v_a\otimes\Omega\rangle=\eta_0e^{is\Delta/\hbar}\sum_j\overline{c_j}\langle h_s,g_j\rangle=\eta_0e^{is\Delta/\hbar}\overline{\langle M,h_s\rangle}$. Integrating with $-i/\hbar$ in the first slot gives the displayed absorption amplitude. Step 1.1 and unitarity give $\alpha_{\mathrm{em}}=-(i\eta_0/\hbar)\int_0^te^{-is\Delta/\hbar}\langle e^{is\varepsilon/\hbar}M,g\rangle ds=-(i\eta_0/\hbar)\int_0^te^{-is\Delta/\hbar}\langle M,h_s\rangle ds$. Since $\eta_0$ is real, conjugating this scalar integral proves $\alpha_{\mathrm{abs}}=-\overline{\alpha_{\mathrm{em}}}$ and equal moduli, including $t=0$ or $\eta_0=0$. This proves (c) for the full complex couplings. [F1, F3, F4, F7, step 1.1, algebra]

[Exact projection probability] Since $H_{0}$ commutes with $Q_{b}$ (both are diagonal in the level basis and $\Pi_1$ is the degree-one Fock-sector projection and the free field group preserves every particle-number sector, [F1], [F4]), [F2] gives $Q_{b}e^{-itH_{\mathrm{LM}}/\hbar}\Psi_{0}=Q_{b}e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}\Psi(t)=e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}Q_{b}\Psi(t)$, so $\|Q_{b}e^{-itH_{\mathrm{LM}}/\hbar}\Psi_{0}\|=\|Q_{b}\Psi(t)\|$ by unitarity. By [F2], $\|\Psi(t)-(\Psi_{0}+\Psi_{1}(t))\|\le\varepsilon_{2}(t)$, and $Q_{b}\Psi_{0}=0$ because $\Psi_{0}$ has no photons ([F4]), so $\|Q_{b}\Psi(t)-Q_{b}\Psi_{1}(t)\|\le\varepsilon_{2}(t)$. [F6] and step 1.1 then give $$\bigl|p_{b}(t)-\gamma_{b}(t)\bigr|\le\varepsilon_{2}(t)\bigl(2\|A_{b}(\cdot,t)\|_{\mathfrak h}+\varepsilon_{2}(t)\bigr),$$ since $\|Q_{b}\Psi_{1}(t)\|=\|A_{b}(\cdot,t)\|$ and $\|Q_{b}\Psi(t)\|\le\|A_{b}(\cdot,t)\|+\varepsilon_{2}(t)$. This proves (b). [F2, F4, F6, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

[Scope and assembly] Steps 1.1 and 2.1 prove (a), step 3.1 proves (b) and step 2.2 proves (c). Only the model's first-order Dyson terms, one projection probability and the finite interval $[0,T]$ entered; neither a rate, a decay, a linewidth, an environment nor a sampling model was formed, and no laboratory identification was made, which is (d). [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 3.1] ∎

claim.text:
Adopt the declared finite-level cutoff dipole model
[[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-finite-level-coupled-model]] and its
spectral-transition reading
[[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-spectral-transition-and-detection]], the
declared ideal energy-window detection model
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-ideal-counting-and-detection-model]] clause (c)
and the preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]). Assume the Axioms of
Countable Choice and of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Declare **three models**, all with the same matter
data $H_{a}$, $D_j^{\mathrm{ch}}$ and the same cutoff $\Lambda$ and coupling
$\eta_{0}$, and with a declared upward level pair $(a,b)$, $\Delta\in(0,\Lambda)$:

1. model $M_{1}$: cutoff mode data whose single-vertex photon density is
   $\nu^{(1)}_{b}=J_{1}\lambda$ with $J_{1}\in L^{1}(\lambda)$, $J_{1}=0$
   $\lambda$-almost everywhere off $(0,\Lambda]$ and $J_{1}$ continuous at
   $\Delta$ with $J_{1}(\Delta)>0$;
2. model $M_{2}$: same matter and cutoff data, single-vertex photon density
   $\nu^{(2)}_{b}=J_{2}\lambda$, $J_{2}$ with the same properties and
   $J_{2}(\Delta)=J_{1}(\Delta)$;
3. model $L$ (the **declared ideal sharp-line model**): a declared spectral
   model in which the energy of an emitted and detected quantum is the value
   $\Delta$ with probability one, so that every energy window
   $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ has probability $\mathbf 1_{B}(\Delta)$.

Assume in addition that $J_{1}$ and $J_{2}$ are **not proportional**: there is
no $\gamma\ge0$ with $J_1=\gamma J_2$ $\lambda$-almost everywhere. The single-vertex laws below are the formal normalized spectral laws of the cited definition for all real $\eta_0$. Their reading as normalized one-photon preparations uses $\eta_0\ne0$; at zero coupling the physical single-vertex vector is zero and no such preparation is formed. No zero-coupling conditioning is asserted. Then:

(a) (equal rate coefficients) the model rate coefficients of clause (c) of
[[pthm-nrqm-light-matter-golden-rule-limit-and-rate-reading]] coincide,
$$\Gamma_{1}=\frac{2\pi\eta_{0}^{2}}{\hbar}J_{1}(\Delta) =\frac{2\pi\eta_{0}^{2}}{\hbar}J_{2}(\Delta)=\Gamma_{2};$$
in particular a comparison of the leading rate coefficients alone does not
discriminate $M_{1}$ from $M_{2}$;

(b) (different detected-energy laws) for every $t>0$ the normalised
single-vertex photon-energy laws $P^{(1)}_{t}$ and $P^{(2)}_{t}$ of clause (e)
of [[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-spectral-transition-and-detection]]
differ: there is a Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ with
$P^{(1)}_{t}(B)\ne P^{(2)}_{t}(B)$; consequently an energy-resolved comparison
that resolves the difference between $J_{1}$ and $J_{2}$ discriminates $M_{1}$
from $M_{2}$, while the rate comparison of (a) does not;

(c) (the sharp line is a limit, not a finite-time property) if $J_{1}>0$
$\lambda$-almost everywhere on a Borel set $B$ of positive Lebesgue measure
with $\Delta\notin B$, then $P^{(1)}_{t}(B)>0$ for every $t>0$ whereas
$L$ assigns probability $0$ to $B$; on the other hand
$P^{(1)}_{t}(B)\to0$ as $t\to\infty$ for every Borel $B$ bounded away from
$\Delta$. Thus the declared sharp-line model is the idealisation that the
single-vertex law approaches in the limit, not a property of the
finite-time law;

(d) (what the comparison is) clauses (a)-(c) are statements about the three
declared models. They construct no laboratory comparison and report no data:
no apparatus, preparation, calibration, detector response, efficiency,
background, trial count, frequency or uncertainty budget is supplied, and
none is invented. Comparing any of these predictions with reported data would
test the combined model and apparatus assumptions under P7, would require a
declared sampling and measurement model, and would carry finite-sample
fluctuations and systematic uncertainties; it would not prove a model.

current_steps.quote: [Equal coefficients] By [F1] and the hypothesis $J_{1}(\Delta)=J_{2}(\Delta)$ one has $\Gamma_{1}=\frac{2\pi\eta_{0}^{2}}{\hbar}J_{1}(\Delta)=\frac{2\pi\eta_{0}^{2}}{\hbar}J_{2}(\Delta)=\Gamma_{2}$. This is (a). [F1, algebra]

[The laws differ] Fix $t>0$ and let $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ be Borel. By [F2], the equality $P^{(1)}_{t}(B)=P^{(2)}_{t}(B)$ for all Borel $B$ would give $K_{t}(E-\Delta)J_{1}(E)=cK_{t}(E-\Delta)J_{2}(E)$ $\lambda$-almost everywhere with $c>0$ as in [F3], and since $K_{t}>0$ $\lambda$-almost everywhere by [F2], division yields $J_{1}=cJ_{2}$ $\lambda$-almost everywhere, contradicting the hypothesis that the densities are not proportional; hence some Borel $B$ separates the two laws. This is (b). [F2, F3, algebra]

[Sharp line] Let $B$ be Borel of positive measure with $J_{1}>0$ $\lambda$-almost everywhere on $B$ and $\Delta\notin B$; by [F2], $P^{(1)}_{t}(B)>0$ for every $t>0$, while $L$ assigns $\mathbf 1_{B}(\Delta)=0$ by [F4]. If in addition $B$ is bounded away from $\Delta$, say $|E-\Delta|\ge\delta$ for every $E\in B$ with $\delta>0$, then $P^{(1)}_{t}(B)\le P^{(1)}_{t}(\{|E-\Delta|\ge\delta\})\to0$ by [F3]. This is (c). [F2, F3, F4, algebra]

[Scope] Clauses (a)-(c) compared three declared models by their model quantities; no apparatus, preparation, calibration, count, frequency or uncertainty entered, and [F5] fixes the status of any later comparison with data as a test of combined assumptions. This is (d). [F5, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3] ∎

**(b) Declared level pair and transition energy.** A **declared level pair**
$(a,b)$ of the model is an ordered pair of orthonormal eigenvectors $v_{a},
v_{b}\in\mathbb C^{d}$ of the compressed matter energy $H_{a}$
([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]],
[[def-inner-product-space]]). Its **transition energy** is
$\Delta:=E_{a}-E_{b}$, read in joules; the pair is **upward** when
$\Delta>0$, meaning level $a$ lies above level $b$ in the model's energy
ordering.

**(c) Dipole coefficients and single-vertex photon density.** For an upward
declared level pair $(a,b)$ and the couplings $D_j^{\mathrm{ch}},g_{j},\eta_{0}$ of
[[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-finite-level-coupled-model]] clauses (c),(d),
the model's **dipole coefficients** are the complex numbers
$$c_{j}:=\bigl\langle D_j^{\mathrm{ch}}v_{a},\,v_{b}\bigr\rangle_{\mathbb C^{d}} \qquad(j=1,\dots,J),$$
the model's **single-vertex mode vector** is
$$M:=\sum_{j=1}^{J}c_{j}\,g_{j}\in\mathfrak h,$$
and the model's **single-vertex photon density** is the finite Borel measure on
$\mathbb R$
$$\nu_{b}(B):=\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}\mathbf 1_{B}\bigl(\varepsilon(k)\bigr)\, \|M(k)\|_{\mathbb C^{3}}^{2}\,d^{3}k,\qquad B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel},$$
read in the model's units and supported in $(0,\Lambda]$. The pairing is linear in its first argument and conjugate-linear in its
second. Thus $c_j$ is the actual coefficient of $v_b$ in $D_j^{\mathrm{ch}}v_a$,
and Hermiticity gives $\langle D_j^{\mathrm{ch}}v_b,v_a\rangle=\overline{c_j}$.
These are exactly the coefficients of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-golden-rule-coefficient-approximate-identity]]
clause (c), with no conjugation or change of the transverse mode vectors;
its mode vector and measure are the present $M$ and $\nu_b$.

**(d) Single-vertex emission vector and coefficient.** For $t\ge0$ the model's
**single-vertex emission vector** is the element of $\mathfrak h$
$$A_{b}(\cdot,t):\quad k\mapsto-\frac{i\eta_{0}}{\hbar}M(k) \int_{0}^{t}e^{i(\varepsilon(k)-\Delta)s/\hbar}\,ds ,$$
and the model's **single-vertex emission coefficient** is
$$\gamma_{b}(t):=\|A_{b}(\cdot,t)\|_{\mathfrak h}^{2}.$$
The vector and the coefficient are **defined model quantities**: the model
assigns them through this clause and through the cutoff dipole mathematics, and
they are not asserted to be the exact probability of any measurement of the
model. In particular $\gamma_{b}(t)$ is dimensionless and is not a rate; the
reading of a rate coefficient requires a separate limit statement, which is not
part of this definition.

**(e) Normalised single-vertex photon-energy law and ideal detection.** For
$t>0$ and $M\ne0$ the model's **normalised single-vertex photon-energy law** is
the Borel probability measure on $\mathbb R$
$$P_{b,t}(B):=\frac{\int_{B}K_{t}(E-\Delta)\,d\nu_{b}(E)} {\int_{\mathbb R}K_{t}(E-\Delta)\,d\nu_{b}(E)},\qquad K_{t}(x):=\frac{1}{\hbar^{2}t}\Bigl|\int_{0}^{t}e^{ixs/\hbar}\,ds\Bigr|^{2},$$
whose denominator is finite and strictly positive by
[[lem-nrqm-light-matter-first-order-photon-energy-law]] clause (b). This
probability law is defined independently of $\eta_0$, including $\eta_0=0$.
Its amplitude-based preparation reading additionally requires $A_b(\cdot,t)\ne0$.
For $t>0$ and $M\ne0$, this is equivalent to $\eta_0\ne0$, since
$\|A_b(\cdot,t)\|^2=\eta_0^2t\int K_t(E-\Delta)\,d\nu_b(E)$ and the integral
is positive. Under this condition the **declared single-vertex
one-photon preparation** is the unit vector $v_{b}\otimes(A_{b}(\cdot,t)/\|A_{b}(\cdot,t)\|_{\mathfrak h})$
of $\mathbb C^{d}\otimes\mathfrak h\subseteq\mathbb C^{d}\otimes
F(\mathfrak h)$, and for a Borel window $B\subseteq[0,\infty)$ the declared
ideal energy-window detector of window $B$ of
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-ideal-counting-and-detection-model]] clause (c)
has the Born probability $P_{b,t}(B)$ in that preparation, because the energy
law of a unit one-photon vector $f$ is the push-forward of
$\|f(k)\|_{\mathbb C^{3}}^{2}d^{3}k$ under $k\mapsto\varepsilon(k)$
([[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]] clause
(e)). When $\eta_0=0$, $A_b(\cdot,t)=0$ and no preparation obtained by
normalizing that emission amplitude is declared; the formal law $P_{b,t}$
remains the probability measure defined above. A **detected photon energy** is therefore a spectral reading of the
assigned free-field energy observable $(H_{f},\mathrm J)$, not a sharp energy
of a normalisable state and not a quantum number of the model's mode labels.

proved statement.
